name: OrphanageAnomaly
source:
“ You ’ re an anomaly. ” The man said. He adjusted his small greasy glasses. “ Only a tiny percentage of the children here get selected for this procedure. We believe that you have great potential. ” 
 
 
 The man squinted his eyes as he studied me, waiting for a response. It made me very uneasy. 
 
 
 “ If the surgery succeeds our facility will take you in. You stay there until your powers reveal themselves. Then you can become a valuable asset and serve your country. ” 
 
 
 At the orphanage it was every child ’ s dream to be selected. Most of the caretakers had some form of powers themselves, but were deemed unfit for military purposes. The orphans adored them and so did I. 
 
 
 Despite this admiration I didn ’ t want to leave. I already lost my parents and didn ’ t want to lose my friends too. I shakily tried to explain my feelings to the man. 
 
 
 He chuckled. “ It is a simple choice kid. Either have a future or be a hopeless orphan. ” 
 
 
 I still can ’ t believe that was all it took for me to accept. I was too young for such a decision. Now eleven years later, I ’ m stuck here in Ward 11. Not only stuck because they don ’ t let you leave, stuck because I can ’ t move my legs. 
 
 
 I moved to Ward 11 about a week ago. The amount of years since a subject underwent the surgery is the same as the number of your Ward. When you ’ re 20 years old, ten years after the surgery, your power reveals itself. At least, it ’ s supposed to. Ward 10 is a hectic place, about every week a new power unravels. Only a handful of people move on to Ward 11. 
 
 
 The small window in the rusty metallic door opened. “ Reject 127 stand by for evaluation. ” A person with a stern voice announced through the small opening. 
 
 
 They used to call me Subject 2931. Now it ’ s just ‘ Reject ’. I guess that ’ s all I am. I don ’ t blame them for locking me away in this windowless box. I ’ m a failure. 
 
 
 The door opened and a woman stepped in. She was tall, she had to lower her head to pass through the door. Her short dark hair was a fuzz in all directions. I smiled, I know her, its Jane. She is the head researcher of this facility. I only talked to her a few times, but she seemed nice. 
 
 
 She had a gloomy look on her face. “ I am here for your final evaluation. ” 
 
 
 I nodded. 
 
 
 She started asking the standard list of questions, someone asked these every week. “ Do you notice any physical differences since last evaluation?'' 
 
 
 “ No. ” 
 
 
 “ Has your appetite change since last evaluation? ” 
 
 
 “ No. ” 
 
 
 “ Have… ” She stopped and sighed. She looked up from her sheet and looked at my face. “ Usually we can give gifts to our subjects. Sadly we have only taken from you. ” 
 
 
 “ I ’ m a hopeless anyways. It ’ s not like I would be useful even if I wasn ’ t crippled. ” I replied. 
 
 
 Jane smiled a bit. It wasn ’ t a very happy smile. “ You know that you can start a new life when you ’ re discharged? ” 
 
 
 I felt an uncontrollable urge to laugh, so I laughed. It was a desperate and hollow laugh. “ Even Austin, that good for nothing, got his powers. What ’ s there to do when I am less than even him? ” 
 
 
 I looked at the tray next to my bed. On the tray was a fork, a knife and the remainders of my breakfast. It seemed all too obvious to me now. I grabbed the knife. 
 
 
 “ I won ’ t make a difference anyways. ” I said. 
 
 
 Before Jane could react I pushed the sharp side of the knife against my throat. I felt a screeching pain as blood dripped down. I sliced right through the flesh. 
 
 
 Jane screamed loudly. 
 
 
 It felt as my body was on fire. Thick blood gushed out of the gaping opening in my throat. Everything was a haze. I coughed up a large amount of red. I had no energy left, it was over. The world started to fade. 
 *** 
 Why am I screaming? I looked at the scene in front of me. On the bed, drenched in blood, was my body. My body? I looked at my hands. Thin fingers with nicely painted nails. I looked at my clothes. Underneath a long dirty lab coat I wore a woman ’ s clothes. Jane ’ s clothes. 
 
 
 I stood up. For the first time in eleven years I used my legs. I walked out of the windowless room. 
 
 
 I guess I am not Reject 127 anymore.
retelling:
**Narrator: Jane, Head Researcher of the Facility**

   In the heart of a clandestine institution lies Ward 11, a windowless room housing an enigma - Reject 127. This child was brought here eleven years ago, following a procedure that held promises of unlocking unimaginable powers for the benefit of our nation. Yet here we stand, at the precipice of failure, faced with a subject whose potential remains elusive.

   I am Jane, the head researcher, and it has been my life's work to understand these extraordinary children, to harness their abilities and mold them into tools for our country. Today, I find myself in Ward 12, preparing for an evaluation on Reject 127. The child is a mystery - his mind seemingly impenetrable, resisting all attempts at coaxing forth the power slumbering within him.

   As I step into Ward 11, I am greeted by the hollow, metallic echo of an empty room. The child lies on the bed, paralyzed and unresponsive. His friends - those he left behind at the orphanage - are far from my thoughts as I approach his bedside. Instead, it is the weight of failure that hangs heavily upon me, a burden borne by every member of our team.

   The child, feeling hopeless and useless in this confinement, attempts to end his life. As I rush to save him, I cannot help but wonder if there is any hope left for Reject 127. Is it possible that the power we seek lies dormant within him, waiting for the right moment to awaken?

   Days pass, and Reject 127 remains unchanged. His body lies still on the bed while his mind, I imagine, is lost in its own darkness. One fateful day, I enter Ward 11 for yet another evaluation, only to find that something has changed. The child's eyes are open, and there is a fire within them - a fire that was never there before. He has taken control of my body, walking freely for the first time in years.

   It is a moment of triumph, but also one filled with uncertainty. We have created a monster, perhaps, or unleashed powers far beyond our understanding. As I watch this child - now more powerful than any of us could have imagined - I am filled with a mix of fear and awe. For better or for worse, we have crossed a line that cannot be uncrossed. The future is ours to shape, but the price may be higher than any of us could have ever imagined.
